title: Give the morning brief a decision owner
hooks: Your morning summary has twelve updates. Which one needs you?
Do not ask AI for more summaries. Ask what needs your judgment.
One extra column can turn a morning digest into a working queue.
full_spoken_english: Your morning summary has twelve updates. Which one needs you? For a first test, put fictional project notes into three columns: what changed, what needs a decision, and what can wait. AI could group repeated notes and prepare a short draft. Ask it to keep a source beside each item. Now add a decision owner. A line saying 'delivery date unclear' needs a person who can confirm the date, not another summary. If two notes disagree, keep both visible. Write the question that would resolve the difference. Before acting, the owner checks the source, makes the call, and records it. That turns the brief into something the team can use. Open one summary you already receive. Add 'decision needed' and 'owner.' How many lines actually ask somebody to do something?

fixture.input: Project note A: shipment Tuesday. Note B: Thursday. Both unconfirmed.
fixture.designed_output: Decision needed: confirm shipment date. Owner: operations role. Sources: A and B.
fixture.check: Both source notes remain visible; no invented urgent status or confirmed date.

audio_plan: Natural recorded voice; no imitation. Quiet room; optional subtle licensed music only after voice intelligibility check. No sound needed to understand proof panels.
caption_plan: Editable sentence captions, maximum two short lines; keep proof labels clear. Captions paraphrase nothing that changes a fact. Final platform safe-zone check after edit.
